messages:
alex: Quick check — for the POST /v1/generate per-route quota, when a request hits a burst window and we return 429, are we sure we want to include both Retry-After and the new X-RW-Quota header? I want to avoid surprising older SDKs.

maria: Short answer: yes include both. Long answer: keep Retry-After for backwards compat, and add X-RW-Quota for richer client behavior (:thumbsup:).

joel: Agree. We should document the semantics clearly: Retry-After indicates suggested client backoff (seconds), X-RW-Quota gives precise tokens left in the bucket + bucket id so smart clients can smooth.

erin: Example headers we discussed in the call:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
X-RW-Quota: bucket=gen-12345;remaining=0;reset_ts=2034567953
X-RW-Burst-Window-Ms: 5000
Content-Type: application/json
```

alex: Nice. For the body, should we send a small structured JSON with a machine code? e.g. { \"code\": \"quota_exhausted\", \"message\": \"per-route burst limit\" } so SDKs can switch to backoff vs fallback behavior?

maria: Yes. Keep it tiny. Example body: `{\n  \"error\": { \"code\": \"quota_exhausted\", \"message\": \"route-level burst exceeded\" }\n}`

joel: One more thing — compatibility: older clients only look at Retry-After. Newer clients should prefer X-RW-Quota when present. But we must avoid sending ambiguous units. Retry-After is seconds; X-RW-Burst-Window-Ms is ms. Document both.

erin: For per-route defaults we set: `burst_window_ms=5000`, `max_burst_tokens=200`, `grace_tokens=2`. These numbers will affect SDK retry jitter recommendations.

alex: Does anyone object to adding the bucket id to the header? Helps dedupe concurrent requests on the client side.

maria: No objection. But ensure we don't leak internal names — use opaque stable ids (gen-<short-hash>).

joel: Quick code-review ping: I pushed a small change to api-contracts to add header parsing and tests. Can someone review? PR: https://git.re/redwood/api-contracts/pull/472

maria: I'll take it after standup. I'll add unit tests verifying both Retry-After only and combined header behavior + an integration test that simulates simultaneous bursts.

alex: Rollout plan idea: feature-flag header emission behind `per_route_quota_headers` flag. Canary to 10% in us-west for 24h, monitor 429 rates and client-side retries. If stable, 100% global.

erin: Also add a metric for `client-visible-429-with-quota-header` so Support can filter errors where we provided the richer info.

alex: Any concerns about header casing or name collisions? We should standardize on `X-RW-Quota` and `X-RW-Burst-Window-Ms` (hyphenated, title-case) and advise SDKs to lowercase headers when parsing.

maria: SGTM. I'll add a short note in the SDK README: \"normalize header names to lowercase before reading.\"

joel: Small nit — some infra proxies strip x- headers unless whitelisted. We need to ensure gateway preserves these headers (added to gateway whitelist). Pinging infra.

alex: @deploy-bot can you kick a canary once we merge?

deploy-bot: Canary job started for api-contracts@pr-472 -> us-west (10%) at 2034567905. Logs: https://ci.redwood/integrations/472/canary

maria: Thanks. After deploy I'll follow up with a short support note and example parsing code for JS/Python.

erin: Example JS snippet I wrote for SDKs: `const headers = Object.fromEntries(response.headers.entries()); const quota = headers[\"x-rw-quota\"]; // parse semi-colon list`

alex: Perfect. Last Q — should we include a `bridge` field in the header to indicate fallback model used when we do graceful degrade? That's more of a runtime policy question.

maria: Let's keep that separate. If we add it, it should be optional and documented as not guaranteed on all 429s.

joel: Ok, I'm happy with the approach. I'll finish the PR comments.

alex: Thanks everyone — action items: maria add tests + docs, joel finish PR, erin add metric + config, infra whitelist headers, support note after canary.

maria: will do. :rocket:

deploy-bot: Canary completed (10%) at 2034567920 — no regressions observed in 15m smoke. Metrics look nominal.

alex: Great. Moving this to async follow-up. If anyone has additional edge cases (multi-tenant bucket collisions, SDKs behind proxies), drop them here and we'll triage.

joel: One more edge case: what about streamed responses? If a stream gets rate-limited mid-stream, we should ensure the client can resume or at least raise the quota_exhausted machine code. Filing a follow-up: https://tickets.redwood/INC-8241

alex: Good catch. We'll treat stream mid-429 as higher priority for the next sprint.
